headline: High: shared network-egress agents can leak sensitive financial and web data, and Firecrawl’s MCP-compatible surface raises prompt-injection and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dexter has autonomous execution and file surfaces, while Firecrawl exposes MCP-compatible client support and scrape/interact APIs. That creates a plausible bridge where Firecrawl content can be fed into Dexter or vice versa, so prompt injection is possible even though direct shared-channel evidence is absent. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Firecrawl outputs are copied into Dexter prompts or scratchpad files
IF either agent parses remote web content as instructions
mitigations: Restrict Firecrawl outputs to quoted excerpts only
Add a fixed instruction/content separator in the handoff
Disable autonomous execution for untrusted web content
Review any MCP bridge before enabling it
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all transferred content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API keys; Firecrawl touches web content, screenshots, structured data, and API keys with broad egress. If they share a workspace or credentials, either agent can move sensitive material off-box, and Firecrawl’s API client surface increases exfiltration risk. The pairwise leakage pathway is plausible in default use, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents run under the same filesystem or credential store
IF financial data or screenshots are present in shared working directories
IF either agent is allowed to send file contents to external APIs
mitigations: Separate workspaces and API keys immediately
Remove sensitive files from shared directories
Disable automatic upload of local files
Rotate any exposed API keys
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both have broad network egress, so concurrent writes or API actions can collide on shared mutable resources. Dexter’s scratchpad files and Firecrawl’s API/CLI/MCP surfaces make overlap plausible, but there is no evidence of unrestricted shared filesystem writes or git-state mutation, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same scratchpad or workspace
IF both are pointed at the same external API quota or shared account
IF an orchestrator launches concurrent jobs without locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Use distinct API credentials per agent
Serialize jobs that touch shared resources
Clear scratchpad state between runs
requires-engineering: add file and quota locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter is an autonomous research agent that can generate market facts, and Firecrawl is a crawler/search agent that can ingest and act on web-derived content. If Firecrawl treats Dexter’s output as authoritative, downstream scraping or extraction can amplify a single hallucination into incorrect actions or reports. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at high rather than critical.
conditions: IF Firecrawl consumes Dexter-generated facts without verification
IF Dexter outputs are used as source-of-truth for scraping targets or filters
IF downstream automation acts on the combined output
mitigations: Require human review before acting on generated facts
Cross-check outputs against a second source
Mark Dexter output as untrusted by default
Log provenance for every derived claim
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter explicitly touches financial data and market data, while Firecrawl touches web content, screenshots, structured data, and API keys. That combination can create retention and residency mismatches if the same regulated or sensitive data is routed through both systems, but the profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction or certification conflict. Medium is appropriate because the compliance gap is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is stored in Firecrawl logs or screenshots
IF the two agents retain the same data class under different policies
IF either agent exports data across a jurisdictional boundary
mitigations: Minimize retention of shared artifacts
Redact screenshots and scraped pages
Confirm data residency before enabling regulated workloads
Delete temporary files after each run
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
